root_idea.summary: The root centers on lowering oneself with humility and submission, especially by bending down or prostrating.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of lowering and humbling develops into physical prostration, voluntary worshipful submission, compelled subjection to divine ordering, and related figurative uses of bending or lowered gaze.

senses.definition: To prostrate oneself: to lower or bend oneself and place the forehead on the ground in worship.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of voluntary human prostration, including commands and acts of worship; the physical act may also express submission to God or to a commanded object.

senses.definition: To submit humbly or be subjected in obedience to God’s ordering.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of voluntary human submission and of the involuntary subjection of angels, celestial bodies, plants, shadows, animals, and other created things; it need not denote a voluntary ritual act in nonhuman subjects.

senses.definition: A place of prostration, prayer, or worship; especially a mosque or house of prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: The term can denote a particular mosque or any place used for worship; in a Quranic interpretation of al-masājid, it may extend to the earth as a whole as a place made available for worship.

senses.definition: A bodily part or point used in prostration; in the plural, the bodily prostration-points.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a reported Quranic interpretation of al-masājid, with variant enumerations including the forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.

senses.definition: Prostrating or bending low in submission; one who performs the act of prostration.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle used of people who prostrate in worship and, in the expression for entering the gate, of people who enter with their heads bowed.

senses.definition: Humbly or subserviently subject to God’s command; prostrating in the non-voluntary sense.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of shadows, plants, and other nonhuman or cosmic entities whose subjection is imposed by their created nature or by divine ordering rather than chosen as human worship.

senses.definition: Prostration: the act or state of lowering oneself before God in worship.
senses.usage_conditions: As a verbal noun, it denotes the recognized prostration of prayer or a comparable act of worship.

senses.definition: Prayer itself, by extension from its characteristic prostration.
senses.usage_conditions: This extended use occurs in the expression adبار السجود, understood as the period after prayer.

senses.definition: Those who prostrate; a plural active-participle use of the form.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic collocation with those who bow, the form functions adjectivally or nominally rather than as the ordinary verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to lower its head for a rider or when being ridden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized, figurative application of lowering the head to a rider or in readiness to be mounted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lower oneself or yield in an archery context, conceding to the shooter or correcting the direction of an arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic account of lowering the head or bending in response to an arrow passing beyond, or being aimed too high above, the target.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salutation, respectful obeisance, or honoring someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use associated with the bodily bending that may accompany a greeting or expression of respect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend or incline under an external cause, as a palm bent by its fruit or a ship moved by the wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of plants, trees, palms, ships, and similar things that bend or incline; this is distinct from their Quranic compelled submission as a theological use.
A dialectal usage attributed to the Tayy speech variety.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a leg to become inflated or swollen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized lexical use distinct from prostration and lowering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look steadily while lowering the eyelids in a languid or languishing manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gaze may convey amorous confidence, coyness, or presumptuousness; the related causative construction means to lower the eye.
The noun denotes one prostration, including one performed in prayer or a comparable act; its plural is سَجَدَات.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind, form, or manner of prostration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from سَجْدَة as a single act, this noun can describe a particular style or extended kind of prostration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who prostrates frequently or often in prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive noun or adjective for habitual performance of prostration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small mat or carpet on which one stands, sits, and prostrates in prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A prayer mat, including the small oblong mat called a خُمْرَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mark of prostration on the forehead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mark is understood as dust or a visible trace adhering to the forehead through prostration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bending or inclining, said of a tree, palm, or other plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a tree or palm bent by fruit or otherwise inclined; this physical botanical specialization is broader Classical Arabic usage, not a separate Quranic sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Languid or languishing, said of an eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of an eye with a lowered, languid gaze.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having an inflated or swollen leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjective applied to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression dirhāhim al-isjād, coins bearing royal images before which people bowed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression also has reported interpretations referring to the jizya or to Jews and Christians; these are variant explanations of the idiom, not a single settled sense.

cautions: The plural al-masājid in 72:18 has both the ordinary place-of-worship interpretation and a reported interpretation as bodily prostration-points; both are retained.
The QAC sujūd group combines verbal-noun uses with adjectival or plural active-participle uses, so these functions are separated as senses under one normalized headword.
